title: Footnote on 'Opus de Funk' and Charlie Shavers's 'Swedish Schapps'
summary: Hughes traces the theme resembling Opus de Funk to Horace Silver and a Shavers composition.

blocks.x: I want to insert a footnote here about the theme that we discussed that sounds like 'Opus de Funk.'
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Opus de Funk was composed by Horace Silver. It was recorded by him with a trio for Blue Note in 1953.
He also recorded it with Milt Jackson and a trumpet player, Henry Boozier on the Prestige label in March 1954.
There's also a version of it on a Savoy record which has Milt Jackson and Frank Wess.
On the Savoy label, the composition is credited not only to Silver, but to B. F. Wood.
Now the Kirby Band featured a composition called "Opus No. 5," but this is not the tune that resembles "Opus de Funk." That is something that comes from Chopin.
The theme that does resemble it is a Charlie Shavers compositon called "Swedish Schapps." As far as I know, he recorded this also in 1953 for the Clef label with Gene Krupa.
